title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving
grouping: Four columns with bold two-line headings across the top (multi-camera features, multi-scale feature aggregation, 3D volume features, occupancy prediction); three scale rows run left to right, with a fourth row added in the volume and prediction columns. A detail panel of the 2D-to-3D block hangs below it inside a thin black frame whose trapezoid lines join the block, and a dashed grey legend box explains the two arrow colours.
shapes_depth: Multi-scale camera features are three stacked levels of thick flat slabs in saturated pastel colours (green, grey, blue, red, purple, yellow) rising from a 2x3 mosaic of camera photos via an orange up-arrow. '2D to 3D' blocks are pale-yellow rounded boxes with 'x6', 'x3', 'x1'. 3D volume features are salmon cube stacks that grow scale by scale (1, 2x2, 4x4, 4x4x deeper) with blue down-arrows between them and shape labels HxWxZ, 2Hx2Wx2Z, 4Hx4Wx4Z, 8Hx8Wx8Z on their output arrows. Each scale ends in a 3-D voxel render of the occupied scene, larger at finer scales. The detail panel is a flat stack of tinted rounded bars (cross-view attention, add & norm, feed forward, 3D convolution) with residual arrows on the right.
proposed_highlight: The predicted occupancy is the visual payload: voxel renders in semantic colours fill the whole right column and grow with resolution; the proposed lifting block is expanded once in the inset rather than coloured differently.
lesson: Show the coarse-to-fine decoder as a column of cube volumes that grow scale by scale with HxWxZ size labels, each feeding a voxel render of the occupancy at that scale, so the multi-scale outputs read as a stack of increasingly detailed 3-D scenes.
notes: Venue ICCV 2023 from the arXiv comment 'Accepted to ICCV 2023' (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref). The whole figure is a single raster image in the PDF (refs crop recorded one embedded image covering the crop), so kb measure cannot separate photos from drawing: photo_share is null and the palette includes the embedded photos and renders.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: four headed columns read left to right (multi-camera features, multi-scale 2D-to-3D aggregation, 3D volume features, occupancy prediction), with the scales running as rows across them

relations.form: four columns under bold headings, joined by straight horizontal arrows from the feature pyramid through the 2D-to-3D blocks to the volumes and their predictions
three scale rows each carry their own '2D to 3D' block (marked x6, x3, x1) from a level of the camera-feature pyramid to a level of the 3D volume stack

3D volume features are salmon cube stacks that grow from a single cube to a 4 x 4 grid, linked top to bottom by short blue '3D deconv' arrows, each emitting an occupancy prediction labelled HxWxZ up to 8Hx8Wx8Z

a black-framed panel below the x1 block, tied to it by two converging lines, opens the 2D-to-3D block as a bottom-to-top stack of cross-view attention, add & norm, feed forward, add & norm and 3D convolution with residual arrows
input is a real 2 x 3 mosaic of camera photos at the bottom left, and each prediction is a voxel render of the scene at its resolution

channels.colour: arrow colour = operation type, keyed in a dashed legend box (orange up arrow = 2D encoder, blue down arrow = 3D deconv); the camera-feature slabs are green, grey, blue, red, purple and yellow without a key; salmon = 3D volume features; in the zoom panel each layer type has its own pastel; voxel colours are semantic classes with no legend in this figure
channels.shape: flat slabs = 2D image features; rounded rectangles = blocks; cube stacks = 3D volumes; voxel renders = outputs
channels.line: black arrows = data flow; short coloured block arrows = the encoder and deconv operations
channels.frame: a black frame = the zoom detail; a dashed grey box = the legend

quality.strengths: The coarse-to-fine 3D volume is drawn as cube stacks that visibly grow down the column, each with its own prediction beside it, so multi-scale supervision is seen as geometry; the 2D-to-3D block is opened in a tied detail panel rather than squeezed into the strip; input and outputs are real data.
quality.weaknesses: Three 2D-to-3D rows feed four volume levels, and the horizontal arrows start in empty space beside the slab pyramid rather than at a specific level, so which feature level feeds which volume is not readable; the six slab colours carry no stated meaning; the volume arrows into the predictions are offset from the cubes they leave; the voxel classes are not keyed here.

insights.structure: Four columns under bold two-line headings (multi-camera features, multi-scale feature aggregation, 3D volume features, occupancy prediction) with scale rows running across, and a black-framed zoom panel of the 2D-to-3D block (cross-view attention, add & norm, feed forward, 3D convolution) hanging below the middle column.
insights.data: Camera images are a real 2 x 3 photo mosaic at bottom left feeding three levels of flat pastel slabs; 3D volume features are salmon cube stacks that grow per scale (1, 2x2, 4x4, larger) with HxWxZ size labels, and outputs are semantic voxel renders that also grow.
insights.emphasis: Growing cube stacks and growing voxel renders show coarse-to-fine resolution at a glance, and the trapezoid zoom lines tie the detail panel to the '2D to 3D' block.
insights.flow: Left to right along each scale row with black arrows; orange up-arrows climb the 2D pyramid and blue down-arrows step down the 3D cube stack, explained by a dashed grey legend box.
insights.avoid: The camera pyramid of overlapping coloured slabs is visually busy and the fourth (finest) scale row has no matching 2D-to-3D block, so the row count does not line up across columns.

arrangement.units: four headed columns without frames; one black-framed detail panel; a dashed-grey legend box
arrangement.inputs_as: a real multi-camera photo mosaic at bottom left
arrangement.shared: the 2D-to-3D block repeats per scale (x6, x3, x1)
